_why:
Fifteen edges flagged as unsourced twins - the same node pair joined twice, one edge sourced and noted at Tier 1, the other bare at Tier 3 with a generic type.

The obvious move was to delete the bare ones as redundant. That would have been wrong. Reading each pair showed the bare type usually asserts something REAL and distinct from its twin: AARO owes Volume II as well as having withheld it; Volume I covers AATIP's lifecycle as well as rejecting the reverse-engineering account; the DIA money went to BAASS as well as BAASS holding its own DUNS and CAGE codes. A pair can carry two relationships and this board's typed edges exist to say so.

What was actually wrong is that nobody had ever articulated what the bare edge asserts. So each now carries a note saying it, drawn from claims already verified and recorded on the two nodes, and the node's own primary sources. No new research and no new assertion - this is the board connecting evidence it already holds.

One of them is worth reading on its own. 50 U.S.C. 3091a(e)(3) defines a controlled access programme as 'a program created or managed pursuant to Intelligence Community Directive 906, or successor directive'. Congress delegated the definition of its own subject to an executive instrument, so what counts as a CAP can be changed without legislation.

The DoDD 5205.07 pair is the one worth reading twice. Its temporal edge records that the 2024 issuance cancels the 2010 one. The programmatic edge records what changed: the 2010 glossary defines 'carve-out' and its Enclosure 2 restates the waiver, and a full-text pass of the 2024 reissue finds no occurrence of 'carve-out', 'waived' or 'unacknowledged'. That is a real and separate finding, and it is why deleting these bare edges as redundant would have cost something. It also does not mean the mechanism ended: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) still carries the carve-out in codified regulation and still names DoDD 5205.07.

edges.note: AARO is the office that OWES this volume, which is a different relationship from having withheld it. Sec. 6802 places the duty on the Director of the Office, and Volume I commits to it twice in its own text: page 6, 'AARO will publish Volume II in accordance with the date established in Section 6802', and page 45, 'This report represents Volume I of AARO's HR2.' The denial edge on this same pair records the non-delivery; this one records whose obligation it is.

edges.note: The report is where the Department's own account of AATIP sits. Volume I records that AAWSAP 'was also known [as] AATIP' and that DIA cancelled the programme in 2012, then that supporters proposed KONA BLUE to DHS as a follow-on. That is the programmatic relation: the report covers the programme's lifecycle. The denial edge on this pair is separate and records the report's rejection of the reverse-engineering account.

edges.note: The report is the object of the search, which is what makes this investigative rather than a denial. A full-text pass of Volume I returns no occurrence of 'Yankee Blue' across all 63 pages including endnotes 1-200. That negative finding is what refuted the widely repeated claim - asserted on this board until 12 August 2026 - that AARO conceded the programme in Volume I.

edges.note: Same policy instrument, two issuances, and the programmatic relation is what CHANGED between them - which is not the same fact as the supersession recorded on the temporal edge. The 2010 directive's glossary defines 'carve-out' as 'a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its National Industrial Security Program oversight', and its Enclosure 2 para 5 restates the statutory waiver in policy. A full-text pass of the 12 September 2024 reissue finds no occurrence of 'carve-out', 'waived' or 'unacknowledged' at all. The vocabulary the earlier directive defined is simply absent from the later one. Note what that does and does not establish: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) still carries the carve-out in codified regulation, and still points at DoDD 5205.07 by name, so the mechanism did not end when the words left the directive.
